question.text: Scenario: Sarvottam Fintech Ltd. (SFL), an unlisted fintech company, plans to launch its IPO. The company's financials for the last three years show: net tangible assets of Rs.5 crore, Rs.4.2 crore, and Rs.3.8 crore; average operating profit of Rs.17 crore (positive each year); and net worth of Rs.2 crore each year. The IPO is structured as a book building issue with a price band of Rs.280-Rs.320 per share. The total issue size is 50 lakh shares, comprising 35 lakh fresh issue shares and 15 lakh shares as Offer for Sale by the promoter, Harish Mehta. The issue receives the following subscription on closing day (T day): QIB category -- 1.5 crore shares bid (against 25 lakh shares reserved); NII category -- 60 lakh shares bid (against 7.5 lakh shares reserved); RII category -- 52.5 lakh shares bid (against 17.5 lakh shares reserved). The cut-off price is determined at Rs.310 per share. Pooja Sharma, a retail investor, applied for 200 shares at cut-off price through ASBA, with funds blocked in her SCSB account. Vikram Desai, the RTA officer, is coordinating the post-issue process. Question 3 of 5: Pooja's RII application of 200 shares at Rs.310 had funds blocked in her SCSB account. The RII category is oversubscribed and, under the retail allotment mechanism (minimum bid lot first, then balance demand), she is allotted 1 lot of 50 shares. Under the ASBA framework, what happens to the funds in her SCSB account?

answer.text: Entire blocked amount of Rs.62,000 is debited and any excess is refunded by cheque from the company
Rs.15,500 is debited for the 50 allotted shares and the balance of Rs.46,500 is unblocked in her SCSB account
All 200 shares are allotted; Rs.62,000 is debited in full
No shares are allotted; Rs.62,000 is refunded by cheque within 15 days

explanation.text: The Logic: Blocked amount = 200 x Rs.310 = Rs.62,000. For 50 shares allotted at Rs.310, the debit is 50 x Rs.310 = Rs.15,500. Under ASBA, the unallotted portion is simply unblocked in the SCSB account, so Rs.62,000 - Rs.15,500 = Rs.46,500 is unblocked. The Trap: Under ASBA there is no refund by cheque from the issuer; funds were only blocked, never debited. Treating the leftover as a "refund" or assuming full allotment of 200 shares both misread the ASBA mechanism described in pages 114 and 118. Note: The retail allotment mechanism on page 98 uses minimum bid lot first and balance-demand rules, not a flat 200 / oversubscription proportional calculation. This question takes the lot allotment as given and focuses on the ASBA debit and unblocking arithmetic.
